content:
Lately, the radar queue has grown extremely large: https://radar.lean-lang.org/queue. In fact, it mostly consists of 295 tau ceti commits that are blocking on runner-lean1. This means that we also only getting benchmarks for builds of lean core (which imo are more important) 2 days later; and it's getting worse and worse! The reason for this is that a radar bench on tau ceti takes around 12 minutes but we're getting more than 6 commits per hour on average on tau ceti so the queue just keeps growing.

The specific benchmarks in question here are those that would usually get reported to the "Significant commits to <repository>" zulip channels and are used as data to determine which changes are considered significant. Now, first of all, I'm not aware of any "Significant commits to TauCeti" zulip channel, so you'd have have to visit the radar website to view these results, which I don't think AIs are going to usually do on their own (unless there is an instruction for that in some .md file I'm not aware of...). Second of all, I think we're getting enough data from commits already; I don't think we need to get a bench of every commit for that.

So, I'd say we should maybe only bench on every third or fourth commit on tau ceti (or even rarer), simply because we're getting so many commits there (and lean core should also get a reasonable slice of the cake).

@Joscha Mennicken

Robin Arnez said:

I'm not aware of any "Significant commits to TauCeti" zulip channel

#Tau Ceti > radar reports
Ah thanks; but still it seems like we're putting way more compute into tau ceti benchmarks than we use
perhaps we could see if three commits together produce a significant change and only if that's the case, check the individual commits
